title: Gaussian-Poisson Limit for Causal Trace Inference at a Singular Bures Corner

proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved the closed-box trace expansion, parameter-free two-way Gaussian–Poisson comparison sharpened to O(n^-1/2), plug-in transfer, and full-parent n^-1 corner interval-length order. Independent reviewers accepted the mathematical proofs and verified all five cited sources; the final contribution was graded incremental below the field floor, with no bounded in-scope upgrade. The exact limiting connected-interval optimization and attaining globally honest transfer remain separate research; F-stage Lean formalization was not launched and no reusable Lean substrate was promoted.
tldr: The central result is a root-\(n\)-accurate two-way original-record Gaussian--Poisson comparison at a singular, nonunique four-projector Bures corner, uniformly on a closed local box including both zero-intensity axes. The identified causal trace has an explicit mixed quadratic/rare-direction expansion and a uniform centered empirical limit. A single count-based interval is \(0.90\)-honest over the full parent \(\Delta_4\) at every \(n\ge2\), and its corner expected length has the optimal order \(n^{-1}\) against all honest randomized connected intervals. General singular trace invariance and conditional count approximation are credited results; the contribution is their precise closed-boundary statistical assembly.
gap: Regular Bures covariance limit theory does not cover this nonunique corner, and comparable-cell Gaussian experiment results do not retain zero or \(n^{-1}\)-mass rare categories. Generic trace invariance, Poisson approximation, and quadratic-bootstrap failure are already known.
fill: The kernel connects explicit value geometry, two-way mixed-count comparison, centered trace inference, and same-parent honest corner length. All are proposed obligations; the general trace identity and classical count tools are credited.
